review_notes: I read the whole file and the related Basic.lean (simp lemma `mem_coinvariants_iff`) and the downstream files HopfBaseChange.lean and Descent.lean. I also read Mathlib's `Subalgebra.baseChange`. I did not run Lean. The finding about the competing rule is an argument from simp's bottom-up traversal order, not an observed failure. The two element-level simp lemmas `coe_coinvariantsBaseChangeEquiv` and `map_coinvariantsBaseChangeEquiv_symm` look consistent. Downstream uses call them with `rw` or `exact`, so their simp status is not exercised. I found no other simp-interface problems.

findings.excerpt:
@[simp]
theorem coinvariants_baseChangeHopfIdeal [Module.Flat R S] (I : HopfIdeal R H) :
    (baseChangeHopfIdeal (K := S) I).coinvariants = I.coinvariants.baseChange S := by
findings.problem: This simp rule competes with the existing simp rule `HopfIdeal.mem_coinvariants_iff`. Simp rewrites subterms before the enclosing proposition. For `z ∈ (baseChangeHopfIdeal I).coinvariants`, the subalgebra term is therefore rewritten first, to `I.coinvariants.baseChange S`. After that, `mem_coinvariants_iff` no longer matches, so the explicit comultiplication/quotient characterization is lost. Mathlib has no simp API for membership in `Subalgebra.baseChange`. It is defined as `AlgHom.range (map (id) C.val)`, so the goal becomes an opaque range-membership statement. The rewrite also needs the `Module.Flat R S` instance, so it only fires conditionally and the normal form of the same expression depends on flatness. The lemma has no simp use in the repository. Downstream code uses the iso and the equiv with `rw` and `exact`, so the attribute gains nothing there.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `@[simp]` from `coinvariants_baseChangeHopfIdeal`, so that `mem_coinvariants_iff` stays the canonical simp normal form for membership. Users can then invoke the lemma explicitly with `rw` or `simp [coinvariants_baseChangeHopfIdeal]`. If a simp-normal membership statement is wanted, add a separate lemma `z ∈ (baseChangeHopfIdeal I).coinvariants ↔ z ∈ I.coinvariants.baseChange S`, or state a `Subalgebra.mem_baseChange`-style characterization, instead of rewriting the subalgebra itself.
findings.benefit: This avoids a conditional rewrite that overrides the existing simp rule `mem_coinvariants_iff` on base-changed coinvariants. Simp goals about membership in `(baseChangeHopfIdeal I).coinvariants` keep their explicit equalizer form. They no longer turn into goals about `Subalgebra.baseChange`, which has no simp API.
